title: Collections: Lists, Dictionaries, Sets and Tuples
oneLiner: Create, add, look up and loop over arrays and lists, dictionaries, sets and tuples in both languages, the modify-while-iterating trap, and the Big O of every common operation.
keyTakeaway: Lists are O(1) by index and for adding at the end, but O(n) to search or to insert at the front. Dictionaries and sets find, add and remove by key in O(1) on average, so a lookup inside a loop belongs in one of them. Assigning a collection to another variable shares it rather than copying it, and changing a collection while looping over it is a bug in both languages.
explanation:
A collection holds many values under one name. Four kinds cover nearly everything you'll write. A list keeps items in order and reaches them by position (index). A dictionary, also called a map, stores pairs of a key and a value and finds the value for a key almost instantly. A set holds unique values and answers "is this in here?" almost instantly. A tuple bundles a small, fixed number of values, such as a name and a reading.

C# has two kinds of list: an array, whose length is fixed when it's created, and List<T>, which grows. The <T> part names the type of item, so a List<int> can only hold ints; that's a generic type. Python's list grows and can hold any mix of types. Dictionary<TKey, TValue> matches Python's dict, and HashSet<T> matches set.

Choosing the right collection is mostly about which operations must be fast. Big O notation describes how the cost of an operation grows with the number of items n: O(1) means constant, however big the collection; O(n) means proportional to its size. Reading a list by index is O(1), but searching a list for a value is O(n), while a dictionary or set lookup is O(1) on average thanks to hashing. The table at the end of this lesson lists the costs for every common operation.

Two mistakes cause most collection bugs: thinking that assigning a list to a new variable copies it (it doesn't, both names share one list), and adding or removing items while looping over the same collection.
